courses.title: ELA 3
courses.description: A literature-rich third-grade English language arts course that integrates reading, writing, word study, grammar and speaking/listening every week. Students read fables, folktales, Greek myths, poetry, biographies and two classic novels (Charlotte's Web and The Wonderful Wizard of Oz), write narratives, informational reports, opinion essays and a short research report, and build decoding with prefixes, suffixes and multisyllable words.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy; 2014 CA ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.3.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text.
standards.RL.3.2: Recount stories, including fables, folktales and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details.
standards.RL.3.3: Describe characters (traits, motivations, feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
standards.RL.3.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
standards.RL.3.5: Refer to parts of stories, dramas and poems using terms such as chapter, scene and stanza; describe how each part builds on earlier sections.
standards.RL.3.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or characters.
standards.RL.3.7: Explain how illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (mood, character, setting).
standards.RL.3.9: Compare and contrast themes, settings and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters.
standards.RL.3.10: Read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.RI.3.1: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of an informational text, referring explicitly to the text.
standards.RI.3.2: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
standards.RI.3.3: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or steps in technical procedures using time, sequence and cause/effect language.
standards.RI.3.4: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a grade 3 text.
standards.RI.3.5: Use text features and search tools (key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information efficiently.
standards.RI.3.6: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
standards.RI.3.7: Use information gained from illustrations (maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding.
standards.RI.3.8: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).
standards.RI.3.9: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
standards.RI.3.10: Read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2–3 band independently.
standards.RF.3.3a: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
standards.RF.3.3b: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
standards.RF.3.4a: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.RF.3.4b: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate and expression on successive readings.
standards.RF.3.4c: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.W.3.1: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons, linking words and a concluding statement.
standards.W.3.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas clearly, with facts, definitions, details, linking words and a conclusion.
standards.W.3.3: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences using descriptive details, dialogue, clear event sequences, temporal words and closure.
standards.W.3.4: With guidance and support, produce writing in which development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
standards.W.3.5: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising and editing.
standards.W.3.6: With guidance and support, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) and to interact and collaborate.
standards.W.3.7: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
standards.W.3.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes and sort evidence into categories.
standards.W.3.10: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of tasks, purposes and audiences.
standards.SL.3.1: Engage effectively in collaborative discussions, coming prepared, following agreed-upon rules, asking questions and explaining their own ideas.
standards.SL.3.2: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media.
standards.SL.3.3: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
standards.SL.3.4: Report on a topic or text, tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
standards.SL.3.5: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading; add visual displays when appropriate.
standards.SL.3.6: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.L.3.1a: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs in general and in particular sentences.
standards.L.3.1b: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.
standards.L.3.1d: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.
standards.L.3.1e: Form and use the simple (I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.
standards.L.3.1g: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, choosing between them.
standards.L.3.1i: Produce simple, compound and complex sentences.
standards.L.3.2c: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.
standards.L.3.2e: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words.
standards.L.3.2f: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts).
standards.L.3.2g: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, to check and correct spellings.
standards.L.3.3a: Choose words and phrases for effect.
standards.L.3.3b: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.
standards.L.3.4a: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
standards.L.3.4b: Determine the meaning of a new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word.
standards.L.3.4c: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root.
standards.L.3.4d: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.
standards.L.3.5a: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).
standards.L.3.5b: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).
standards.L.3.5c: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty.
standards.L.3.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic and domain-specific words, including words signaling spatial and temporal relationships.

objectives: Establish a daily independent reading routine
Recount fables and state the moral

days.title: Reading launch
days.work: Choose a library book for a 20-minute independent reading routine and start a reading log; read 'The Lion and the Mouse' and discuss its moral.

days.title: Recount a fable
days.work: Read 'The Tortoise and the Hare,' retell it in 5 sentences using first/next/then/finally, and spell closed vs. open syllable words (rab-bit, ti-ger).

days.title: Sentence types
days.work: Learn the four sentence types and end punctuation; find each type in 'The Fox and the Crow' and write one of each about the fable.

days.title: Writing a memory
days.work: Brainstorm small-moment memories and draft a half-page narrative about a time you learned a lesson.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a spelling check on syllable types, answer 4 text-based questions on a new fable, and discuss its lesson aloud using complete sentences.

weeks.assessment: Fable comprehension questions, spelling check, narrative draft

objectives: Describe characters' traits and how actions lead to a lesson

days.title: Character traits
days.work: Read 'The Ant and the Grasshopper' and fill a trait chart for each character with text evidence.

days.title: Vowel teams
days.work: Sort and spell ai/ay and ee/ea words, then read 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' aloud for fluency.

days.title: Nouns
days.work: Identify common and proper nouns in 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' and write 5 sentences using both.

days.title: Narrative leads
days.work: Revise the first paragraph of your personal narrative with a strong lead (action, dialogue or sound).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how one character's actions taught the moral, then partner-discuss which fable lesson matters most.

weeks.assessment: Character paragraph with evidence; noun practice sheet

objectives: Compare lessons in folktales from different cultures

days.title: Anansi tales
days.work: Read an Anansi the Spider folktale and identify the trickster's problem, choices and lesson.

days.title: Stone Soup
days.work: Read a version of 'Stone Soup' and chart how the villagers change from start to end; spell r-controlled words (ar, or, er, ir, ur).

days.title: Plural nouns
days.work: Practice regular (-s, -es) and irregular plurals (mouse/mice, child/children) with a sorting activity and sentences.

days.title: Revise for detail
days.work: Add sensory details and feelings to the middle of your personal narrative, using a revision checklist.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare the lessons of Anansi and Stone Soup in a Venn diagram and discuss with a family member.

weeks.assessment: Venn diagram comparison; plural nouns check

days.title: Abstract nouns
days.work: Learn abstract nouns (kindness, courage, friendship) and identify the abstract noun each fable teaches about.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit your narrative for capitals, end punctuation and plurals; practice prefixes un- and re- in spelling.

days.title: Ending
days.work: Write a satisfying ending that reflects on the lesson learned, then publish a final copy.

days.title: Fluency
days.work: Practice reading a fable aloud 3 times for expression and record yourself.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Read a new fable and answer questions on moral and character, take the un-/re- spelling test, and read your narrative aloud.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 reading assessment; published narrative scored with rubric

objectives: Ask and answer questions with text evidence

days.title: Chapters 1–2
days.work: Read chapters 1–2 and describe Fern's character with evidence; discuss whether Fern's father was fair.

days.title: Chapter 3–4
days.work: Read chapters 3–4 and write 3 questions and answers about Wilbur's loneliness; spell dis- and pre- words.

days.title: Verbs
days.work: Identify action and linking verbs in a passage from chapter 4 and write 6 sentences about the barn.

days.title: Chapter 5
days.work: Read chapter 5 and describe first impressions of Charlotte using a character web.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a chapters 1–5 quiz and a prefix spelling check (dis-, pre-, mis-).

objectives: Explain how characters' actions move the plot

days.title: Chapters 6–7
days.work: Read chapters 6–7 and explain how Wilbur learns his fate and how it changes the plot.

days.title: Verb tenses
days.work: Write sentences about the novel in past, present and future tense; spell -ful and -less words.

days.title: Chapters 8–9
days.work: Read chapters 8–9 and explain how each chapter builds on the last in a plot chart.

days.title: Story plan
days.work: Plan an original animal story with a story map (characters, setting, problem, events, solution).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how Charlotte's plan begins and take a verb tense quiz.

objectives: Determine meanings of words and phrases

days.title: Chapters 11–12
days.work: Read chapters 11–12 and discuss why the web words ('Some Pig') work; list strong words Charlotte chooses.

days.title: Irregular verbs
days.work: Practice irregular past tense verbs (spin/spun, write/wrote, catch/caught) using sentences about the book; spell -ly and -ness words.

days.title: Chapters 13–14
days.work: Read chapters 13–14 and figure out the meaning of 5 tricky words from context.

days.title: Draft story
days.work: Draft the beginning and middle of your animal story with at least 2 lines of dialogue.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an irregular verbs quiz and answer comprehension questions on chapters 11–15.

days.title: Chapters 16–17
days.work: Read chapters 16–17 (the fair) and describe Templeton's motivation.

days.title: Dialogue punctuation
days.work: Copy dialogue from the novel and learn quotation mark and comma rules; spell words with -ed and -ing using the doubling rule.

days.title: Chapters 18–19
days.work: Read chapters 18–19 and chart how Wilbur has changed since chapter 1.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise your story's dialogue for correct punctuation and temporal words (later, meanwhile).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a dialogue punctuation check and discuss Charlotte's sacrifice in a family book talk.

weeks.assessment: Dialogue punctuation check; book talk participation

weeks.topic: Charlotte's Web, chapters 20–22 and story publishing
objectives: Determine the theme of the novel

days.title: Chapters 20–22
days.work: Finish the novel and discuss the theme of friendship and the cycle of life.

days.title: Theme
days.work: Write a paragraph stating the novel's theme supported by 2 quotations; spell drop-e words (hope/hoping).

days.title: Publish
days.work: Edit and publish your animal story with illustrations.

days.title: Book talk
days.work: Give a 2-minute book talk recommending Charlotte's Web to a friend.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 2 test (comprehension, vocabulary, verbs, dialogue) and share your published story.

objectives: Use text features to locate information

days.title: Text feature hunt
days.work: Find headings, captions, bold words, glossary and index in an animal nonfiction book and explain each feature's job.

days.title: Main idea
days.work: Read a ReadWorks passage on camouflage and identify the main idea and 3 supporting details.

days.title: Adjectives
days.work: Identify adjectives in animal descriptions and write 5 descriptive sentences; spell change-y-to-i words (cry/cries).

days.title: Choose an animal
days.work: Select an animal for an informational report and write 5 questions you want to answer.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer text-feature questions on a new passage and take the spelling check.

weeks.assessment: Text feature check; main idea organizer

objectives: Describe cause/effect relationships in scientific texts
Compare a pourquoi tale to fact
materials: Just So Stories by Rudyard Kipling (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Just So Story
days.work: Read Kipling's 'How the Leopard Got His Spots' and discuss how a pourquoi tale explains nature.

days.title: Real reasons
days.work: Read a nonfiction passage on leopard camouflage and complete a cause/effect chart.

days.title: Comparatives
days.work: Use comparative and superlative adjectives (faster, fastest) to compare animal features; spell -able and -ible words.

days.title: Note taking
days.work: Take notes on your report animal from 2 sources, sorting facts into body, habitat, food and adaptations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph comparing the fiction and nonfiction explanations of the leopard's spots.

weeks.assessment: Fiction vs. nonfiction paragraph; notes check

days.title: Report plan
days.work: Organize notes into an outline with an introduction, 3 topic paragraphs and conclusion.

days.title: Diagrams
days.work: Study a labeled diagram of an animal and explain what it adds to the words; spell -tion and -sion words.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft introduction and first two paragraphs using linking words (also, another, and, but).

days.title: Commas
days.work: Practice commas in a series and in addresses by writing a letter to a zoo asking a question.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finish the report draft and read it to a family member for feedback on clarity.

weeks.assessment: Report draft; letter with correct comma use

objectives: Revise and publish an informational report with a text feature

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the report for definitions of key words and a strong conclusion; spell -ment and -er/-or words.

days.title: Add text features
days.work: Add a heading, labeled diagram, caption and glossary to the published report.

days.title: Video listening
days.work: Watch a short nature video on your animal and note main ideas and details.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your report to the family and answer 3 questions.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 3 test on main idea, text features and cause/effect with a new passage.

objectives: Recount a myth and determine its lesson
materials: A Wonder-Book for Girls and Boys by Nathaniel Hawthorne (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: What is a myth?
days.work: Learn about Ancient Greece and the Olympian gods, then make a gods chart with symbols.

days.title: Pandora
days.work: Read the Pandora myth ('The Paradise of Children') and recount it in sequence.

days.title: Agreement
days.work: Practice subject-verb agreement with sentences about the gods; study Greek roots (bio, graph, photo).

days.title: Lesson
days.work: Write what lesson the Pandora myth teaches about curiosity.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a subject-verb agreement quiz and answer questions on the Pandora myth.

objectives: Begin opinion writing about a text

days.title: King Midas
days.work: Read 'The Golden Touch' and chart Midas's wishes, actions and consequences.

days.title: Arachne
days.work: Read the myth of Arachne and Athena and describe Arachne's pride with evidence.

days.title: Pronouns
days.work: Practice pronoun-antecedent agreement in sentences about both myths; spell diphthongs oi/oy, ou/ow.

days.title: Opinion plan
days.work: Plan an opinion paragraph: Which character learned the hardest lesson? Give 2 reasons.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write the opinion paragraph with linking words and discuss it in a book talk.

days.title: Persephone
days.work: Read the Persephone myth and explain how it explained the seasons.

days.title: Illustrations
days.work: Compare two illustrations of Icarus and explain how each shows mood.

days.title: Icarus
days.work: Read the Icarus myth and discuss nonliteral phrases like 'flying too close to the sun.'

days.title: Capitalize titles
days.work: Write the titles of all myths and books read so far with correct capitalization; spell homophones (their/there/they're).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions about both myths and listen to a family member's retelling, asking 3 questions.

days.title: Myth plan
days.work: Plan an original myth explaining a natural event (why the moon changes shape) with a story map.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the myth using a god or hero character and dialogue; spell irregular words (said, laugh, though).

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise the myth for a clear lesson and strong verbs.

days.title: Present
days.work: Read the myth aloud with expression to an audience.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 4 test on myths, agreement and capitalization.

objectives: Use poetry terms to describe parts of poems
materials: A Child's Garden of Verses by Robert Louis Stevenson (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Stanzas
days.work: Read Stevenson's 'My Shadow' and label lines and stanzas; describe what each stanza adds.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Clap the rhythm of 'The Swing' and practice reading it aloud with expression; spell VCCV multisyllable words.

days.title: Literal vs. nonliteral
days.work: Find nonliteral phrases in poems and draw literal vs. real meanings.

days.title: Write a poem
days.work: Write a rhyming poem in 2 stanzas about a shadow or swing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record a fluent reading of a Stevenson poem and complete a poetry terms check.

objectives: Explain how word choice creates images
materials: 'Who Has Seen the Wind?' by Christina Rossetti
'April Rain Song' by Langston Hughes (library anthology)

days.title: Rossetti
days.work: Read 'Who Has Seen the Wind?' and sketch the images the poet creates.

days.title: Hughes
days.work: Read 'April Rain Song' and list sensory words; spell VCV words (cab-in, ti-ger).

days.title: Shades of meaning
days.work: Order related words on a line (whisper, say, shout; think, believe, know).

days.title: Free verse
days.work: Write a free-verse poem about weather using sensory words.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing how one poet's word choice creates a feeling.

weeks.assessment: Word choice response; shades of meaning check

objectives: Create an audio recording of poems

days.title: Word connections
days.work: Describe people and places in your life with words from the poems (cozy, gentle, noisy).

days.title: Poem types
days.work: Read and write an acrostic and a cinquain; spell consonant-le words (table, puzzle).

days.title: Anthology
days.work: Compile 6 favorite poems (3 published, 3 original) into an illustrated anthology.

days.title: Record
days.work: Record a poetry podcast reading 3 poems fluently.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Complete a poetry test on terms, nonliteral language and imagery.

weeks.assessment: Unit 5 test; poetry anthology and recording

objectives: Describe a sequence of events in a person's life
materials: The Story of My Life by Helen Keller (Project Gutenberg, chapter 4 excerpt)

days.title: Biography basics
days.work: Compare biography and autobiography; start a timeline of Helen Keller's life.

days.title: Primary account
days.work: Read the water-pump excerpt from 'The Story of My Life' and discuss how she felt.

days.title: Conjunctions
days.work: Combine sentences about Helen Keller using and, but, or, so; spell over-, under-, sub- words.

days.title: Main idea
days.work: Identify the main idea of a biography chapter and its key details.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete the timeline and write a summary of Helen Keller's achievements.

weeks.topic: Biography: Ruby Bridges and Jackie Robinson
objectives: Distinguish own point of view from the author's
materials: The Story of Ruby Bridges by Robert Coles (library)

days.title: Ruby Bridges
days.work: Read 'The Story of Ruby Bridges' and discuss the courage she showed.

days.title: Jackie Robinson
days.work: Read a Jackie Robinson biography and list challenges he faced.

days.title: Subordinating conjunctions
days.work: Write complex sentences with because, when, although, after; study Latin roots port and rupt.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare the two people's challenges and actions in a chart; write how your view differs from the author's.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Hold a discussion on 'What is courage?' using evidence from both texts.

objectives: Write an opinion essay with reasons from texts
Write simple, compound and complex sentences

days.title: Opinion choice
days.work: Choose which person showed the greatest courage and list reasons with evidence.

days.title: Organizer
days.work: Plan an essay with introduction, 3 reasons with evidence and conclusion; study roots struct and tract.

days.title: Sentence variety
days.work: Practice simple, compound and complex sentences about your person.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the essay with linking words (because, therefore, for example).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read the draft to a partner and get 2 compliments and 1 suggestion.

objectives: Revise and type an opinion essay

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise reasons and conclusion using the opinion rubric.

days.title: Type it
days.work: Type the final essay, practicing keyboarding; study Greek roots tele, phon, scope.

days.title: Speech
days.work: Turn the essay into a 2-minute speech with note cards.

days.title: Deliver
days.work: Deliver the speech to family, speaking clearly and making eye contact.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Complete the Unit 6 test on biographies, conjunctions and sentence types.

days.title: Chapters 1–2
days.work: Read chapters 1–2 and contrast Kansas and Oz with descriptive details.

days.title: Chapters 3–4
days.work: Read chapters 3–4 and describe the Scarecrow; spell silent-letter words (kn, wr, gh).

days.work: Use comparative and superlative adverbs (faster, most carefully) in sentences about the journey.

days.work: Read chapters 5–6 and write whether you agree with the Tin Woodman's view that a heart matters most.

days.work: Complete a chapters 1–6 quiz and a point-of-view journal entry.

days.work: Study 3 Denslow illustrations and explain what they show about mood and character.

days.work: Take a possessives quiz and write a character trait paragraph.

days.title: Chapters 16–18

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math 3
courses.description: Third-grade mathematics focused on the four critical areas of the CA framework: multiplication and division within 100, fractions as numbers (especially unit fractions), area, and two-dimensional shapes. Students also round, add and subtract within 1,000, solve two-step word problems, measure time, mass and liquid volume, and represent data with scaled graphs and line plots.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.3.OA.A.1: Interpret products of whole numbers as the total number of objects in equal groups (5 x 7 as 5 groups of 7).
standards.3.OA.A.2: Interpret whole-number quotients as the number in each share or the number of shares (56 ÷ 8).
standards.3.OA.A.3: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems with equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.
standards.3.OA.A.4: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.3.OA.B.5: Apply properties of operations (commutative, associative, distributive) as strategies to multiply and divide.
standards.3.OA.B.6: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
standards.3.OA.C.7: Fluently multiply and divide within 100; know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers by the end of grade 3.
standards.3.OA.D.8: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations; represent with equations using a letter for the unknown; assess reasonableness with estimation.
standards.3.OA.D.9: Identify arithmetic patterns (including in the addition and multiplication tables) and explain them using properties of operations.
standards.3.NBT.A.1: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
standards.3.NBT.A.2: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value and properties of operations.
standards.3.NBT.A.3: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90.
standards.3.NF.A.1: Understand a fraction 1/b as one part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b.
standards.3.NF.A.2: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
standards.3.NF.A.3: Explain equivalence of fractions and compare fractions by reasoning about their size (same numerator or same denominator); express whole numbers as fractions.
standards.3.MD.A.1: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes; solve elapsed-time word problems.
standards.3.MD.A.2: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses using grams, kilograms, and liters; solve one-step word problems with these units.
standards.3.MD.B.3: Draw scaled picture graphs and scaled bar graphs to represent data with several categories; solve one- and two-step 'how many more/less' problems.
standards.3.MD.B.4: Generate measurement data with rulers marked in halves and fourths of an inch; show the data on a line plot.
standards.3.MD.C.5: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement using unit squares.
standards.3.MD.C.6: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).
standards.3.MD.C.7: Relate area to multiplication and addition; use tiling, side-length multiplication, the distributive property, and decomposition of rectilinear figures.
standards.3.MD.D.8: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including unknown side lengths and rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas (or vice versa).
standards.3.G.A.1: Understand that shapes in different categories may share attributes; recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as quadrilaterals.
standards.3.G.A.2: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

units.title: Place Value, Rounding, Add & Subtract within 1000
units.big_idea: Place value lets us round, estimate, and add or subtract large numbers efficiently.

units.title: Meaning of Multiplication and Division
units.big_idea: Multiplication joins equal groups; division splits a total into equal groups or finds the number of groups.

units.title: Multiplication Strategies and Fact Fluency
units.big_idea: Properties of operations let us use facts we know to find facts we don't.

units.title: Area
units.big_idea: Area measures how much flat space a shape covers and connects to multiplication.

units.title: Two-Step Problems and Patterns
units.big_idea: Good problem solvers represent, solve, and check for reasonableness.

units.title: Fractions as Numbers
units.big_idea: Fractions are numbers made of equal-size unit parts and live on the number line.

units.title: Time, Liquid Volume and Mass
units.big_idea: We measure with standard units and use operations to solve measurement problems.

units.title: Data: Scaled Graphs and Line Plots
units.big_idea: Graphs organize data so we can compare and answer questions.

units.title: Geometry and Perimeter
units.big_idea: Shapes are classified by attributes; perimeter is the distance around a shape.

units.title: Year Review and Fluency Celebration
units.big_idea: Connecting the year's big ideas shows what we know and can do.

days.title: Division fluency

days.work: Take a two-step problem quiz and explain one solution with a bar model.

courses.subject: SCI
courses.title: Science 3
courses.description: A hands-on, NGSS-aligned third-grade science course covering forces and motion, magnets and static electricity, life cycles, animal groups, inheritance and variation, fossils, habitats and environmental change, weather and climate, and weather-related hazards. Students conduct investigations with household materials, keep a science notebook, construct evidence-based arguments, and complete engineering design challenges.
courses.framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 CA Science Framework

standards.3-PS2-1: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
standards.3-PS2-2: Make observations and/or measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
standards.3-PS2-3: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
standards.3-PS2-4: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets.
standards.3-LS1-1: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction and death.
standards.3-LS2-1: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
standards.3-LS3-1: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
standards.3-LS3-2: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
standards.3-LS4-1: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of the organisms and the environments in which they lived long ago.
standards.3-LS4-2: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates and reproducing.
standards.3-LS4-3: Construct an argument with evidence that in a particular habitat some organisms can survive well, some survive less well, and some cannot survive at all.
standards.3-LS4-4: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
standards.3-ESS2-1: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
standards.3-ESS2-2: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
standards.3-ESS3-1: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard.
standards.3-5-ETS1-1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time or cost.
standards.3-5-ETS1-2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints.
standards.3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

units.title: Forces and Motion
units.big_idea: Pushes and pulls change motion when forces are unbalanced, and patterns of motion can be predicted.

units.title: Magnets and Static Electricity
units.big_idea: Some forces act at a distance; we can use magnets to solve problems.

units.title: Life Cycles
units.big_idea: All living things are born, grow, reproduce and die, but their life cycles differ.

units.title: Animal Groups and Survival
units.big_idea: Living in groups helps some animals survive.

units.title: Inheritance, Variation and Environment
units.big_idea: Offspring inherit traits from parents, traits vary, and environment can influence traits.

units.title: Fossils and Past Environments
units.big_idea: Fossils are evidence of organisms and environments from long ago.

units.title: Habitats and Environmental Change
units.big_idea: Organisms survive best in habitats that meet their needs; when environments change, solutions can help.

units.title: Weather and Climate
units.big_idea: Weather follows seasonal patterns that can be measured, and climates differ around the world.

units.title: Natural Hazards and Engineering Design
units.big_idea: Engineers design solutions that reduce the impacts of weather-related hazards.

days.title: Review & check

days.title: Analyze

days.title: Review & check

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: Continuity and Change (Local History)
courses.description: Third-grade history–social science focused on the student's own region: its physical geography, the American Indian nations who have lived there since long ago and today, the explorers, missions, ranchos and settlers who changed it, and how the local community was founded and has changed over time. Students also learn about rules, laws, citizenship and the three branches of government, national symbols and heroes, and the local economy, using maps, photographs, oral histories and other primary sources.
courses.framework: California History–Social Science Content Standards; 2016 CA History–Social Science Framework

standards.3.1: Students describe the physical and human geography and use maps, tables, graphs, photographs and charts to organize information about people, places and environments in a spatial context.
standards.3.1.1: Identify geographical features in their local region (deserts, mountains, valleys, hills, coastal areas, oceans, lakes).
standards.3.1.2: Trace the ways in which people have used the resources of the local region and modified the physical environment (dams, cultivation, buildings).
standards.3.2: Students describe the American Indian nations in their local region long ago and in the recent past.
standards.3.2.1: Describe national identities, religious beliefs, customs and various folklore traditions of local American Indian nations.
standards.3.2.2: Discuss the ways in which physical geography, including climate, influenced how local Indian nations adapted to their natural environment (food, clothing, tools).
standards.3.2.3: Describe the economy and systems of government, particularly those with tribal constitutions, and their relationship to federal and state governments.
standards.3.2.4: Discuss the interaction of new settlers with the already established Indians of the region.
standards.3.3: Students draw from historical and community resources to organize the sequence of local historical events and describe how each period of settlement left its mark on the land.
standards.3.3.1: Research the explorers who visited here, the newcomers who settled here, and the people who continue to come to the region, including their cultural and religious traditions and contributions.
standards.3.3.2: Describe the economies established by settlers and their influence on the present-day economy, with emphasis on private property and entrepreneurship.
standards.3.3.3: Trace why their community was established, how individuals and families contributed to its founding and development, and how it has changed over time, drawing on maps, photographs, oral histories, letters, newspapers and other primary sources.
standards.3.4: Students understand the role of rules and laws in our daily lives and the basic structure of the U.S. government.
standards.3.4.1: Determine the reasons for rules, laws and the U.S. Constitution; the role of citizenship in promoting rules and laws; and the consequences for people who violate rules and laws.
standards.3.4.2: Discuss the importance of public virtue and the role of citizens, including how to participate in a classroom, in the community and in civic life.
standards.3.4.3: Know the histories of important local and national landmarks, symbols and essential documents that create a sense of community among citizens and exemplify cherished ideals (flag, bald eagle, Statue of Liberty, Constitution, Declaration of Independence, U.S. Capitol).
standards.3.4.4: Understand the three branches of government, with an emphasis on local government.
standards.3.4.5: Describe the ways in which California, the other states and sovereign American Indian tribes contribute to the making of our nation and participate in the federal system of government.
standards.3.4.6: Describe the lives of American heroes who took risks to secure our freedoms (e.g., Anne Hutchinson, Benjamin Franklin, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, Frederick Douglass, Harriet Tubman, Martin Luther King Jr.).
standards.3.5: Students demonstrate basic economic reasoning skills and an understanding of the economy of the local region.
standards.3.5.1: Describe the ways in which local producers have used and are using natural, human and capital resources to produce goods and services in the past and the present.
standards.3.5.2: Understand that some goods are made locally, some elsewhere in the United States and some abroad.
standards.3.5.3: Understand that individual economic choices involve trade-offs and the evaluation of benefits and costs.
standards.3.5.4: Discuss the relationship of students' 'work' in school and their personal human capital.

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Art & Music 3
courses.description: Third-grade visual art and music alternating in units. In art, students explore line, shape, color, value, texture, pattern, printmaking and sculpture through observation and imagination, study artists and cultures, and curate an exhibition. In music, students read and write rhythms and melodies, sing with solfege, explore instruments and music of California and the world, and compose and perform original music.
courses.framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools (Visual Arts and Music); 2020 CA Arts Education Framework

standards.MU:Pr5.1.3: Apply teacher-provided and collaboratively developed criteria and feedback to evaluate and refine performances.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.3: Perform music with expression and technical accuracy, demonstrating performance decorum and audience etiquette appropriate for the context and venue.
standards.MU:Re7.1.3: Demonstrate and describe how selected music connects to and is influenced by specific interests, experiences or purposes.
standards.MU:Re7.2.3: Demonstrate and describe how a response to music can be informed by the structure, the use of the elements of music and context (personal and social).
standards.MU:Re8.1.3: Demonstrate and describe how the expressive qualities (dynamics, tempo, timbre) are used in performers' and personal interpretations to reflect expressive intent.
standards.MU:Re9.1.3: Evaluate musical works and performances, applying established criteria.
standards.MU:Cn10.1.3: Demonstrate how interests, knowledge and skills relate to personal choices and intent when creating, performing and responding to music.
standards.MU:Cn11.1.3: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts and daily life.

units.title: Line, Shape and Observational Drawing
units.big_idea: Artists use line and shape to record what they observe and imagine.

units.title: Rhythm and Meter
units.big_idea: Music is organized in steady beats and rhythmic patterns we can read, write and create.

units.title: Color and Painting
units.big_idea: Artists mix and choose colors to create mood and meaning.

units.title: Melody, Pitch and Singing

units.title: Printmaking, Texture and Pattern
units.big_idea: Printmaking repeats images to create pattern and texture.

units.title: Music of California and the World

units.title: Sculpture and Form

objectives: Use a variety of lines expressively

days.title: Line hunt
days.work: Find 10 kinds of lines in your home and draw each in a sketchbook line chart.

days.title: Line in art
days.work: Look at a Van Gogh painting ('The Starry Night') and describe how the lines show movement.

days.title: Feelings in lines
days.work: Draw lines to show calm, angry, excited and sleepy to music.

days.title: Line design
days.work: Create a full-page line design using at least 8 line types.

days.title: Review & sing
days.work: Share the line design and sing a warm-up echo song keeping a steady beat.

objectives: Draw from observation using contour line

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Draw your hand three times without looking at the paper, moving the pencil slowly with your eyes.

days.title: Still life
days.work: Arrange 3 pieces of fruit and draw their outer and inner contour lines from observation.

days.title: Add detail
days.work: Return to the still life and add texture lines, shadows and a table edge to make it more realistic.

days.title: Shoe drawing
days.work: Draw a sneaker from observation, including laces, stitching and tread patterns.

days.title: Review
days.work: Lay out week 1 and week 2 drawings side by side and write 2 ways your observation improved.

objectives: Use geometric and organic shapes in compositions

days.title: Shape sort
days.work: Cut 20 shapes from scrap paper and sort them into geometric and organic groups.

days.title: Matisse
days.work: Look at Henri Matisse's paper cut-outs (e.g., 'The Snail') and speculate how he made them.

days.title: Cut-paper collage
days.work: Create a Matisse-inspired collage of organic shapes cut freehand from painted paper.

days.title: Kandinsky
days.work: Listen to a lively orchestral piece and make a geometric composition of circles, lines and triangles inspired by Kandinsky.

days.title: Review
days.work: Give a 1-minute artist talk explaining the shapes you chose and why.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Combine two animals into an imaginary creature and list where it lives, what it eats and its special power.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Sketch the creature using basic shapes first, then contour lines.

days.title: Elaborate
days.work: Add a detailed habitat background and at least 3 patterns or textures.

days.title: Final
days.work: Finish the drawing with colored pencil, layering light to dark.

days.title: Unit 1 check
days.work: Self-assess with a line/shape/detail checklist and clap the syllable rhythm of your creature's name.

days.title: Beat vs. rhythm
days.work: Pat the steady beat on your knees while singing 'Yankee Doodle,' then clap the rhythm of the words.

days.title: Body percussion
days.work: Perform a 4-beat body percussion pattern (stomp, pat, clap, snap) to a steady beat.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Walk, jog and tiptoe to recorded music at slow, medium and fast tempos.

days.title: Echo
days.work: Echo-clap 10 four-beat rhythm patterns played by a parent or recording.

days.title: Review
days.work: Perform the beat on a bucket drum while a family member claps the rhythm, then switch.

objectives: Read and write quarter notes, eighth notes and quarter rests

days.title: Notes
days.work: Learn quarter notes ('ta') and paired eighth notes ('ti-ti') and read 8 flash cards aloud.

days.title: Rests
days.work: Add the quarter rest and clap rhythms where the rest is a silent open-hand gesture.

days.title: Read
days.work: Read and clap 8 four-beat rhythm cards, then play them on a bucket drum.

days.title: Dictation
days.work: Listen to 5 clapped rhythms and write each one with stick notation.

days.title: Review
days.work: Clap a 6-card rhythm quiz with no mistakes.

materials: recordings of a march and a waltz

days.title: Half note
days.work: Learn half notes and half rests and clap rhythms that combine them with quarters.

days.title: Conducting
days.work: Conduct 2-beat, 3-beat and 4-beat patterns to a march, a waltz and a pop song.

days.title: Measures
days.work: Draw bar lines into 6 written rhythms in 4/4 and 3/4 time.

days.title: Waltz
days.work: Listen to Strauss's 'The Blue Danube' and sway on beat 1 of each measure.

days.title: Review
days.work: Identify the meter of 4 recordings and complete a bar-line worksheet.

days.title: Improvise
days.work: Answer a parent's 4-beat clapped 'question' with your own improvised 4-beat 'answer' 10 times.

days.title: Ostinato
days.work: Create a repeating ostinato on a pot or bucket to accompany 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat.'

days.title: Compose
days.work: Compose a 4-measure rhythm piece in 4/4 time using stick notation and Chrome Music Lab Rhythm.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Assign household percussion to each line and rehearse your piece 3 times.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Perform the composition for family and explain how you organized the rhythms.

objectives: Mix primary into secondary and intermediate colors

days.title: Primary colors
days.work: Mix red, yellow and blue on a palette to make orange, green and violet; record recipes.

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Paint a 6-color wheel on a paper plate.

days.title: Intermediate
days.work: Mix and add the 6 intermediate colors (red-orange, yellow-green, etc.) to make a 12-color wheel.

days.title: Brush care
days.work: Practice wash, dry-brush and stipple strokes, then clean and store brushes correctly.

days.title: Review
days.work: Label all 12 colors on the wheel and explain how to mix any one of them.

objectives: Use warm and cool colors to create mood

days.title: Sort
days.work: Sort paint chips or magazine scraps into warm and cool color groups.

days.title: Picasso
days.work: Look at Picasso's 'The Old Guitarist' and describe the mood the blue colors create.

days.title: Warm landscape
days.work: Paint a simple landscape using only warm colors.

days.title: Cool landscape
days.work: Paint the same landscape again using only cool colors.

days.title: Review
days.work: Display both paintings and write 3 sentences comparing their moods.

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Paint a 7-step value scale by adding white (tints) and black (shades) to one color.

days.title: Monochromatic
days.work: Paint a small monochromatic picture of a tree using only one color plus white and black.

days.title: O'Keeffe
days.work: Look at Georgia O'Keeffe's close-up flower paintings and discuss why she painted them so large.

days.title: Flower painting
days.work: Paint a large close-up flower that fills the page, using at least 4 tints and shades.

days.title: Review
days.work: Explain where you used light and dark values and how they create form.

weeks.assessment: Value scale and O'Keeffe-inspired flower painting

days.title: Listen and paint
days.work: Paint freely while listening to Smetana's 'The Moldau,' letting colors follow the river music.

days.title: Dynamics
days.work: Learn forte (loud) and piano (soft) and sing a song using both.

days.title: Contrast
days.work: Paint two small pieces to a calm piece and an energetic piece of music.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Explain how colors in each painting match the music's dynamics and tempo.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Choose your best painting and score it on a color-use rubric.

objectives: Identify high and low pitch and melodic direction

days.title: Pitch sort
days.work: Listen to 10 sounds and sort them as high or low.

days.title: Direction
days.work: Draw the up-down contour of 'Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star' as a line.

days.title: Body levels
days.work: Sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' showing pitch with hand levels.

days.title: Melody maps
days.work: Draw melody maps for 2 short songs and play them on a keyboard app.

days.title: Review
days.work: Complete a listening quiz identifying melodies that go up, down or stay the same.

objectives: Sing with solfege syllables and Curwen hand signs

days.title: Sol-mi
days.work: Learn sol and mi hand signs and sing 'Rain, Rain, Go Away' with them.

days.title: Adding la
days.work: Add la and sing 'Ring Around the Rosie' with hand signs.

days.title: Do-re-mi
days.work: Add do, re and mi and sing the pentatonic scale up and down.

days.title: Folk song
days.work: Sing a pentatonic folk song ('Bow Wow Wow' or 'Hot Cross Buns') in solfege.

days.title: Review
days.work: Echo-sing 8 solfege patterns with correct hand signs.

objectives: Read pitches on the treble staff

days.title: Staff
days.work: Learn the 5 lines and 4 spaces and draw a treble clef 5 times.

days.title: Note names
days.work: Learn E-G-B-D-F (lines) and F-A-C-E (spaces) with a mnemonic.

days.title: Write
days.work: Write 10 notes on the staff from letter names.

days.title: Read and play
days.work: Read and play 'Hot Cross Buns' (E-D-C) on a keyboard app from notation.

days.title: Review
days.work: Complete a 15-note naming quiz.

objectives: Use dynamics and tempo to convey intent

days.title: Dynamics
days.work: Sing 'This Land Is Your Land' with forte, piano, crescendo and decrescendo.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Sing a lullaby at a slow tempo and a march at a fast one and discuss why.

days.title: Compare performances
days.work: Compare two recorded versions of the same song and describe the differences in expression.

days.title: Expression plan
days.work: Mark dynamics on a song sheet to match the meaning of its words.

days.title: Review
days.work: Perform the song with your marked expression for family.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a chosen song, recording yourself once.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Listen to the recording with a parent and choose 2 things to fix (pitch, words, dynamics).

days.title: Compose
days.work: Compose an 8-beat melody using do-re-mi-sol-la in Chrome Music Lab Song Maker.

days.title: Etiquette
days.work: Discuss performer and audience etiquette (bow, listen quietly, applaud).

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Perform the song and your melody for family using proper concert etiquette.

days.title: Rubbings
days.work: Make crayon rubbings of 10 textured surfaces (leaves, coins, screens, bark).

days.title: Visual texture
days.work: Draw 6 textures (fur, bark, scales, feathers, brick, water) in a sketchbook grid.

days.title: Dürer
days.work: Look closely at Albrecht Dürer's 'Young Hare' and speculate how he painted each hair.

days.title: Texture collage
days.work: Cut your rubbings into shapes to build a textured animal collage.

days.title: Review
days.work: Present the collage and name the texture used for each part.

objectives: Create repeating patterns through relief printmaking

days.title: Patterns
days.work: Photograph or sketch 5 patterns found in fabrics, tiles and nature.

days.title: Stamp prints
days.work: Carve potato or sponge stamps and print an alternating pattern border.

days.title: Foam plate
days.work: Draw a design firmly into a foam tray with a pencil to make a print plate.

days.title: Print edition
days.work: Roll paint onto the plate and print an edition of 3 prints, signing and numbering each.

days.title: Review
days.work: Choose your best print and explain why using criteria (clear lines, even ink).

objectives: Explain how cultures tell stories through printed art

days.title: Adinkra
days.work: Learn about Ghanaian adinkra cloth and the meanings of 6 symbols.

days.title: Personal symbols
days.work: Design 3 personal symbols that represent your family values.

days.title: Symbol cloth
days.work: Print your symbols in a grid on fabric or paper using stamps.

days.title: Hokusai
days.work: Look at Hokusai's woodblock print 'The Great Wave' and discuss how prints spread stories.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Present your symbol cloth and explain what each symbol means.

materials: recording of Britten's 'Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra'

days.title: Families
days.work: Learn the 4 orchestra families and how each makes sound.

days.title: Britten
days.work: Listen to Britten's 'The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra' and raise a card for each family.

days.title: Timbre game
days.work: Identify 10 instruments by sound alone in a listening game.

days.title: Make an instrument
days.work: Build a shoebox rubber-band guitar and explore how band thickness changes pitch.

days.title: Review
days.work: Complete an instrument family quiz.

objectives: Explore music from California's cultures and history

days.title: Mariachi
days.work: Listen to mariachi music and identify the violin, trumpet, vihuela and guitarrón.

days.title: California Indian song
days.work: Listen to a California Indian song recording from a tribe or museum website and discuss its purpose.

days.title: Gold Rush songs
days.work: Learn and sing 'Oh My Darling, Clementine' and discuss what it tells about miners' lives.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare instruments, tempo and purpose of the three styles in a chart.

days.title: Review
days.work: Write a paragraph about the style you connected to most and why.

days.title: Taiko
days.work: Watch a Japanese taiko performance and copy a simple taiko rhythm with large arm motions.

days.title: Gamelan
days.work: Listen to Indonesian gamelan and describe its layered, repeating patterns.

days.title: Djembe
days.work: Learn bass, tone and slap strokes and a West African call-and-response rhythm on a bucket.

days.title: Music map
days.work: Mark each music tradition on a world map with a drawing of its main instrument.

days.title: Review
days.work: Discuss how each style reflects the culture and purpose that created it.

objectives: Choose and perform a folk song from another culture

days.title: Choose
days.work: Choose a folk song from another culture (e.g., 'De Colores,' 'Sakura,' 'Funga Alafia') and explain your choice.

days.title: Learn
days.work: Learn the words and melody, including their meaning.

days.title: Accompany
days.work: Add a simple percussion accompaniment that fits the song's style.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform the folk song for family, introducing where it comes from.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: Reflect in writing on what went well and what you'd practice next time.

objectives: Create 3D forms in clay using pinch and coil methods

days.title: Shape vs. form
days.work: Compare a drawn circle to a ball and roll basic forms (sphere, cylinder, cube) in clay.

days.title: Pinch pot
days.work: Make a pinch pot with even walls by pressing and turning.

days.title: Coil pot
days.work: Build a coil pot, joining coils with score-and-slip.

days.title: Texture
days.work: Add carved or pressed textures to both pots with household tools.

days.title: Review
days.work: Evaluate the pots for even walls and secure joins.

objectives: Create a sculpture from found and recycled materials

days.title: Nevelson
days.work: Look at Louise Nevelson's assemblage sculptures and discuss how painting them one color unifies them.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Collect recycled materials and sketch a plan for a free-standing sculpture.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the sculpture, testing balance as you add pieces.

days.title: Paint
days.work: Paint the whole sculpture one color to unify it.

days.title: Review
days.work: Present the sculpture and view it from all sides with family.

objectives: Construct a map and model of a familiar place

days.title: Choose
days.work: Choose a familiar place (bedroom, park, kitchen) and list its important features.

days.title: Map
days.work: Draw a bird's-eye-view map of the place with a key.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build a 3D cardboard model of the place based on your map.

days.title: Details
days.work: Add small details (furniture, trees, signs) from paper and clay.

days.title: Unit 7 check
days.work: Evaluate the model using criteria (accurate, detailed, sturdy) and give a tour.

objectives: Improvise melodic ideas for a purpose

days.title: Question-answer
days.work: Play a 4-beat melodic 'answer' to a parent's melodic 'question' on a keyboard app.

days.title: Pentatonic
days.work: Improvise freely on black keys (pentatonic) over a steady drum beat.

days.title: Story music
days.work: Improvise music for a story scene (storm, sneaking, celebration).

days.title: Record
days.work: Record your 3 best improvisations.

days.title: Review
days.work: Listen back and choose a favorite idea to develop into a song.

objectives: Compose and notate a short song

days.title: Lyrics
days.work: Write 4 lines of lyrics about a topic you care about.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Set the lyrics to rhythms using quarter, eighth and half notes.

days.title: Melody
days.work: Create a melody for the rhythm in Song Maker, ending on do.

days.title: Notate
days.work: Write the song in standard or iconic notation.

days.title: Review
days.work: Share the draft and explain how the music fits the words.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Play your song for a family member and collect 2 'glows' and 1 'grow.'

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise rhythm or melody based on the feedback and document changes.

days.title: Practice
days.work: Practice performing the revised song with steady tempo.

days.title: Accompaniment
days.work: Add a percussion ostinato accompaniment.

days.title: Review
days.work: Compare the original and revised versions and explain which is better and why.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse your song 3 times with accompaniment.

days.title: Program notes
days.work: Write program notes explaining your song's meaning and how you made it.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform the premiere for family, reading your program notes first.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Watch a recording and score it on criteria (steady beat, accurate pitch, expression).

days.title: Unit 8 check
days.work: Write a reflection on the whole composing process.

objectives: Explain how cultures record history through art

days.title: Rivera murals
days.work: Look at a Diego Rivera mural and identify the story it tells about workers.

days.title: Chumash rock art
days.work: View images of Chumash rock paintings and discuss what they may mean and why they must be protected.

days.title: Context
days.work: Discuss how knowing when and where an artwork was made changes your response to it.

days.title: Plan mural
days.work: Sketch a mural plan showing important people and places in your community.

days.title: Review
days.work: Share the mural sketch and get feedback.

objectives: Create a mural representing your community

days.title: Grid transfer
days.work: Draw a grid on your sketch and the butcher paper to scale up the design.

days.title: Draw
days.work: Draw the design lightly onto the large paper.

days.title: Background
days.work: Paint the sky, land and large background shapes.

days.title: Details
days.work: Paint people, buildings and details, using tints and shades.

days.title: Review
days.work: Evaluate the mural with family and add finishing touches.

objectives: Select and prepare artwork for exhibition

days.title: Select
days.work: Review the year's portfolio and select 6 best works.

days.title: Mat
days.work: Mount each artwork on a construction paper mat.

days.title: Artist statements
days.work: Write a 3-sentence artist statement for each selected work.

days.title: Plan the space
days.work: Compare a hallway wall and a digital slideshow gallery as exhibit spaces and choose one or both.

days.title: Review
days.work: Arrange the exhibit layout and make labels.

days.title: Program
days.work: Choose 4 songs from the year (including your original song) for a concert.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the songs learned in units 4 and 6.

days.title: Rehearse original
days.work: Rehearse your original song with accompaniment.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Run the full program in order with introductions.

days.title: Review
days.work: Design and print a concert program.

objectives: Present an art exhibit and concert

days.title: Set up
days.work: Hang the art exhibit and set up a performance area.

days.title: Gallery walk
days.work: Lead family on a gallery walk, explaining each artwork.

days.title: Concert
days.work: Perform the concert program.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Evaluate one artwork and one song using criteria from the year.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write about your growth as an artist and musician this year.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: PE 3
courses.description: Third-grade physical education building locomotor, balance, jump rope, throwing, catching, dribbling, striking and dance skills through daily active practice. Students learn the components of health-related fitness, measure heart rate, complete baseline and end-of-year fitness checks, set goals, and practice cooperation, strategy and fair play in small-sided games.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards; 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-3.1.1: Perform smooth transitions between sequential locomotor skills (e.g., running into a jump).
standards.PE-3.1.2: Jump for distance and height, landing on both feet with hips, knees and ankles bent to absorb force.
standards.PE-3.1.3: Balance on, move along and dismount from a line or low beam with control; hold balances on different bases of support.
standards.PE-3.1.4: Perform a forward roll and other rolling actions safely with control.
standards.PE-3.1.5: Jump a self-turned rope repeatedly using a variety of footwork patterns.
standards.PE-3.1.6: Jump a long rope turned by others, entering and exiting.
standards.PE-3.1.7: Throw an object overhand with accuracy and appropriate force toward a target.
standards.PE-3.1.8: Catch thrown objects at different levels (above head, at waist, below waist) and while moving.
standards.PE-3.1.9: Dribble a ball with the hand while walking and running, changing direction and speed.
standards.PE-3.1.10: Dribble a ball with the feet and kick a ball to a stationary or moving target.
standards.PE-3.1.11: Strike an object with a paddle or racket using forehand motion, and strike a stationary ball with a bat.
standards.PE-3.1.12: Perform simple folk, line and creative dances in time to music.
standards.PE-3.2.1: Explain the key elements of overhand throwing, catching, kicking and dribbling.
standards.PE-3.2.2: Explain how force, levels, directions and pathways affect movement.
standards.PE-3.2.3: Explain and apply simple offensive and defensive strategies (open space, guarding) in small-sided games.
standards.PE-3.2.4: Explain how practice and feedback improve skill.
standards.PE-3.3.1: Participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity for increasing periods of time.
standards.PE-3.3.2: Demonstrate muscular strength and endurance (curl-ups, push-ups, plank).
standards.PE-3.3.3: Demonstrate flexibility of major muscle groups (sit-and-reach, shoulder stretch).
standards.PE-3.3.5: Measure and record heart rate before, during and after activity.
standards.PE-3.4.1: Identify the components of health-related fitness (aerobic capacity, muscular strength, endurance, flexibility, body composition).
standards.PE-3.4.2: Explain how the heart, lungs and muscles respond to physical activity.
standards.PE-3.4.3: Explain the purpose of warm-up and cool-down activities.
standards.PE-3.4.4: Set a personal fitness goal and track progress.
standards.PE-3.4.5: Explain how healthy food and water fuel physical activity.
standards.PE-3.5.1: Work cooperatively with a partner or small group to complete tasks.
standards.PE-3.5.2: Accept responsibility for one's actions and demonstrate fair play.
standards.PE-3.5.3: Encourage others and give positive, specific feedback.
standards.PE-3.5.4: Follow safety rules and use equipment properly.
